content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired: eu-west-az2 inference pool - sustained 5xx spike >= 30% over 5m. healthcheck failures and pod restarts. auto-escalation to oncall. runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/az-outage

pagerduty: Alert: PD-4932 - eu-west-az2 serving errors. Pager duty notes attached.

Olivia: acked. I'm oncall for the shift, jumping in. tagging SRE.

Sam: on it. started collecting quick telemetry. can someone confirm if this is 503s from frontend or 500s from runtime?

Raj: logs look like OOMKill + liveness probes failing across g4 pools in az2. autoscaler thrashing - nodes coming up then getting evicted. paste: ```syslog: kubelet: killing process: oom_kill process=python mem=28G```

Emily: Console shows 40% of requests to eu-west routed to az2 and latency going from 120ms -> 1.8s and error rate spike. Snapshot: /console/metrics?range=5m

Olivia: impact? any customers affected? Dedicated EU tenants?

Support Bot: Active incidents: 3 customer-facing errors reported (tickets #7342, #7345, #7349). Customers on Dedicated eu-west are seeing intermittent 503s. No SSO or billing issues reported.

Sam: first mitigation: shift traffic away from az2 to az1 for eu-west region. initiating gradual reroute policy. Command: ```reroutectl set-policy --region eu-west --priority az1,az3 --deprioritize az2 --weight-adjust -30%```

Raj: autoscaler saturation looks like padding config + bad kernel memory growth in a library. I'll disable autoscaler scaling up for az2 until we stabilize to avoid thrash: ```kubectl annotate hpa inference -n infra pause-scaling=true --region=eu-west-az2```

Olivia: PD note - acknowledging root alert and starting failover. Sam take lead for routing, Raj for infra, Emily for console/customer comms.

pagerduty: PD Event: Alert acknowledged by Olivia (oncall). Escalation to SRE team. Next escalation timer paused.

Sam: traffic move started. routing moving 50% of new sessions off az2 in 2 waves. will monitor errors.

(5m later)
Sam: errors dropping to 12% now. latency for eu-west aggregate back to ~180ms but az2 still noisy. continuing reroute.

Raj: found root cause candidate: a lib change in the container image pulled during last deploy that increases jemalloc fragmentation leading to OOM under specific seq-length patterns. reverting image tag on az2 pool. Command: ```k8s-deploy rollback inference-svc --namespace infra --to-tag v1.12.3```

Emily: updating status page: "We are experiencing elevated error rates in eu-west-az2. Traffic is being routed to other availability zones. Mitigation in progress." pinging account managers for 2 impacted Dedicated customers.

Support Bot: Customer #AcmeCorp reported decreased throughput. Reply template ready: "We're routing traffic away from the affected availability zone and investigating. We'll update within 30 minutes."

Olivia: Sam/Raj, confirm whether we should fully cut az2 or keep it in warm standby? I'm leaning warm standby to reduce cold-start risk.

Sam: keep warm standby. we'll reduce weight to 5% and mark unhealthy in LB so no new long-running sessions. Command: ```lbctl set-target-weight eu-west az2 5 --mark-unhealthy```

Raj: rollback finished, we restarted pods. verifying memory growth. logs: ```grep -i oom /var/log/kubelet.log | tail -n 20``` show no new OOMs after restart.

(10m later)
Sam: steady state: eu-west errors now 1.8% region-wide, az2 component about 6% but serving only 5% of traffic. latency good. PD: reducing urgency.

pagerduty: PD Note: incident status updated to "Mitigated" by Olivia. Keep monitoring for full recovery.

Emily: posting interim incident note to #general and product channels. asking support to keep customers informed.

Support Bot: Two customers confirmed degradation stopped after reroute. Tickets updated and marked "monitoring".

Olivia: handing off to Sam for extended monitoring. Sam, take primary for post-mortem and follow-up action items.

Sam: acknowledged. I'll open an incident postmortem and list immediate actions: 1) revert lib change across clusters, 2) add memory limits and OOM guardrails, 3) refine autoscaler cooldown, 4) add alert to detect jemalloc pattern.

Raj: action: create a canary rollout avoidance guard so we don't roll the problematic tag to low-memory pools. Filing PR to infra repo.

Olivia: thanks all. closing PD escalation but leaving thread open for follow up notes.

(End of thread)
